subject: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

messages.author: 8fbd627556b30d4e
messages.subject: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative
parts:
Hi All, 

I am getting this error in Lavaan, where I try to estimate a measurement and structural model. I have used the estimator "ML", the CFI and TLI are a bad fit representing 0.79,0.82 respectively. 

I am using an underlying theory ("Theory of planned behavior"), the dataset is from the survey to validate the theory based on the survey data. 

The sample size of the observation is 42. What could be the possible problem? is it due to sample size or negative e covariance of an item in a latent variable? if so, what is the possible way to resolve it? 

Here is the piece of the code: 

 M_model_EVO <-
 'Attitude =~ ATB1 + ATB2 + ATB3
  PBC =~ PBC1+ PBC2 + PBC3 + PBC4 + PBC5 + PBC6
  SubNorms=~ SN1 + SN2 + SN3 + SN4 + SN5
  EConcern =~ EC1 + EC2 + EC3
  EVOIntent =~ RPI1 + RPI2 + RPI3
 ## Structural Model ##
    PBC ~ EVOIntent  
   Attitude ~ EVOIntent  
   SubNorms ~   EVOIntent
   EConcern  ~ EVOIntent
 '

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative
parts:
Hi Yashi

I took a look at your model and tried fitting it with simulated data. I obtain the same error and a bad fit as well with a sample of 42 observations.

Regarding the bad fit. If I choose to simulate a larger data set (e.g., 100), then the fit measures become better.

Regarding the error. I tried using bounded estimation and it resolved the error (though it is typically used in cases of nonconvergence). You might want to have a look at the paper and use it. Paper: https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2021.1982716

Have a look at the code I provided below. One warning about the simulated data: it may be different and 'easier' to  fit then your own data.

I hope this helps finding out the problem.

Best wishes,

Jasper Bogaert
PhD student and teaching assistant
Department of Data Analysis (PP01)
Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences
Ghent University
​

---------------------------

code:

### load packages
library(lavaan)
library(semPlot)

### specify model
model <- '

Attitude =~ ATB1 + ATB2 + ATB3
PBC =~ PBC1+ PBC2 + PBC3 + PBC4 + PBC5 + PBC6
SubNorms=~ SN1 + SN2 + SN3 + SN4 + SN5
EConcern =~ EC1 + EC2 + EC3
EVOIntent =~ RPI1 + RPI2 + RPI3

PBC ~ 1*EVOIntent  
Attitude ~ 1.5*EVOIntent  
SubNorms ~   0.3*EVOIntent
EConcern  ~ 1*EVOIntent
'

n <- 42 # choose sample size
dat <- simulateData(model, sample.nobs = n) # you might need to resimulate the data untill you get the error

### fit model without bounds
fit <- sem(model, data = dat)
summary(fit, fit.measures = T, standardized = T)
lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")

semPaths(fit)

### fit model with bounds
fit.bounds <- sem(model, data = dat, bounds = "standard")
summary(fit.bounds, fit.measures = T, standardized = T)
lavInspect(fit.bounds, "cov.lv")
